title: Villagers stage Jal Satyagraha against nuclear plant in Rewa

tea.why: Tribal residents and villagers are protesting against a proposed nuclear power plant in their area.
tea.want: Cancel the proposed nuclear power plant project in Rewa district.
tea.changed: Oct 25: Opposition leader Umang Singhar visited the protest site, pledged support, and announced financial aid for a protester's family.

summary: Tribal residents and other villagers have been staging a Jal Satyagraha protest in Sirmour, Rewa district, to oppose a proposed nuclear power plant in Sarai-Rojhouhi villages. Protesters argue that the project poses serious safety, health, and nuclear pollution risks to the densely populated area and threatens tribal lands and rights. On Sunday, Leader of Opposition Umang Singhar visited the protest site to express support, promising to raise the issue in the assembly and block the project's implementation. Singhar also visited the family of a protester, Vimla Kol, whose health reportedly deteriorated during the agitation before her death, and announced financial assistance.
demands: Cancel the proposed nuclear power plant in Rewa district
response: No official response reported in the sources.

deaths.text: Vimla Kol, whose health deteriorated during the agitation before her death

updates.text: Opposition leader Umang Singhar visited the protest site in Sirmour and met with protesting villagers and tribal residents.
Singhar announced Rs 1 lakh in financial assistance for the family of a protester who died after her health deteriorated during the agitation.

sources.title: Singhar backs Rewa villagers’ protest against nuclear plant
